# Choosing a look (bleach bypass, warm film, cool night, vintage, high-key, noir, pastel, punchy, golden hour)

- Kind: `recipe`
- Category: `studio`
- Slug: `studio/looks-catalog`

## Summary

Darkroom recipe (basic). Match the look to the story: `bleach-bypass` (gritty, low saturation, high contrast: war, sport), `warm-film` (nostalgic), `cool-night` (blue night scenes), `vintage` (faded home movie), `high-key` (bright, clean: beauty, product), `noir` (black and white, hard contrast), `pastel` (soft, airy), `punchy-social` (bright saturated phone-screen pop), `golden-hour` (sunset warmth), `moody` (dark, muted).

## Details

### When to use
The user names a mood rather than settings.
### What a pro does and why
Apply to all clips so the edit feels consistent.
### Ops
```json
{
  "summary": "Warm film look",
  "reason": "You asked for a warm film look: a built-in look at moderate intensity",
  "ops": [
    {"op": "apply_look", "clipIds": "all", "lookId": "warm-film", "intensity": 0.8}
  ]
}
```
Swap `lookId` for any look named above; the same op with another id replaces the feel. Examples: `{"op":"apply_look","clipIds":"all","lookId":"bleach-bypass","intensity":0.7}`, `{"op":"apply_look","clipIds":"all","lookId":"cool-night","intensity":0.8}`, `{"op":"apply_look","clipIds":"all","lookId":"vintage","intensity":0.7}`, `{"op":"apply_look","clipIds":"all","lookId":"high-key","intensity":0.6}`, `{"op":"apply_look","clipIds":"all","lookId":"noir","intensity":1}`, `{"op":"apply_look","clipIds":"all","lookId":"pastel","intensity":0.7}`, `{"op":"apply_look","clipIds":"all","lookId":"punchy-social","intensity":0.8}`, `{"op":"apply_look","clipIds":"all","lookId":"golden-hour","intensity":0.7}`, `{"op":"apply_look","clipIds":"all","lookId":"moody","intensity":0.7}`.
### How to adjust
Every look has `intensity` 0 to 1: "too much" = lower it by 0.2. Two looks fight each other: undo the first.
